summary: Marcel Hofinger worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Liège, the Catholic University of Louvain (KU Leuven) under Étienne Lamotte, and the Sorbonne. He held professorial posts at KU Leuven and Université catholique de Louvain (c. 1955–1983).

Marcel Mauss was a religious studies scholar and philosopher educated at Bordeaux, EPHE, Leiden, Utrecht, and Oxford, studying under Émile Durkheim, Sylvain Lévi, and others. He held chairs at the EPHE (1901, 1914–1940) and the Collège de France (1931–1941).

Marcelle Lalou was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Sorbonne and EPHE under Lévi, Bacot, Pelliot, and Przyluski. She served as directeur d’études at EPHE (1938–1963) and chief editor of the Journal Asiatique (1950–1966).

Marco Ferrante works in Indology and philosophy, having completed his BA and PhD at Sapienza University of Rome. He held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (2013–2018, 2020–2025), Oxford (2018–2020), and the University of Vienna (2017–2025).
Marco Franceschini is an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Turin. He served at the University of Bologna as assistant professor (attested 2007–2019) and associate professor (2021).

Marco Trombetta is a scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at Seoul National University (2009–2023) and held a post at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation.
Marco Walther is a Tibetologist who completed his PhD at the University of Munich under the supervision of Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Marco della Tomba was an Indologist and religious studies figure. He served as a missionary in the Tibet-Hindustan Mission (1757–1773) and later held the posts of propraefectus (1786) and praefectus (1801) of the Tibet Mission.

Marcus Bingenheimer works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and computational fields. He studied at Würzburg, Nagoya under Yasuhisa Matsumura, and Heidelberg. His posts include Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts (2005–2011) and Temple University (professor 2012–2015).

Marcus Joseph Müller was a scholar of Iranian/Central Asian studies, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Munich under Othmar Frank, Leiden, and Paris, later serving as professor of non-biblical Oriental literature at Munich (1840, 1847).

Marek Mejor is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Warsaw under Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz. He held a fellowship at Wolfson College, Oxford (1981–1982), and served as professor at the University of Warsaw (attested 2000–2010).

Marek Zemánek is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Dongguk University, Seoul National University, and Charles University, where he completed his dissertation under Radek Chlup.
Marek Zvelebil was an archaeologist who studied at the University of Sheffield (c. 1972–1976) and later held an academic post there (c. 1981–2011).
Margaret Cone is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who was affiliated with the University of Cambridge and Darwin College, Cambridge (attested 1996).
Margaret Elizabeth Noble worked in religious studies and Indology. She was educated at Halifax Ladies' College and studied under Swami Vivekananda in 1898.
Margaret Gouin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed her PhD at the University of Bristol under Paul Williams.

Margaret H. Dornish is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Yale, Claremont Graduate University, and USC. She served as associate professor of religion at Pomona College (attested 1989).

Margaret Mead was an anthropologist who studied at Barnard and Columbia under Franz Boas. She held long-term posts at the American Museum of Natural History (1926, 1946–1969) and taught ethnology at Columbia University (1954–1978).

Margaret R. Miles is a scholar of religious studies and history who studied at SFSU and the GTU. She held positions at Harvard Divinity School (c. 1978–1996) and served as dean of the Graduate Theological Union (1996–2001).

Margarethe Steiner was an Indologist who completed her PhD at the University of Tübingen under Richard von Garbe in 1926. She also studied under Jakob Wilhelm Hauer and held a post at Tübingen in 1939.
